title: Integrated Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's operating procedures across budgeting & forecasting, procurement, contracts (legal process), and revenue recognition & billing. It is intended as the single-source operational guide for finance, legal, procurement, and partnering teams. Use the sections below for processes, approval matrices, templates, and key controls.

Purpose and scope:

- Purpose: Reduce cycle time for purchasing and contracting while ensuring consistent accounting treatment, compliance with internal controls, and predictable forecast accuracy.
- Scope: Applies to all Redwood legal entities and product lines for purchases, contracts, and revenue that affect P&L, balance sheet, or customer invoicing. Excludes purely personal reimbursements (see expense policy).

Key owners and contacts:

- Document owner: Finance - Contract & Revenue Ops (owner_team: finance-legal)
- Primary contacts: Maya Chen (Finance), Priya Nandakumar (Legal), Jordan Lee (Procurement)
- Escalation: Head of Finance (finance@redwood.example.com) -> General Counsel -> CFO

1) Budgeting & forecasting (annual + rolling):

Summary:
- We run an annual planning cycle with quarterly rolling forecasts and monthly variance analysis. Forecasts feed capacity planning (GPU fleet), hiring plans, and Dedicated/Private product pricing decisions.

Calendar & cadence:

1. Annual planning kickoff: May 1 (owner: FP&A)
2. Preliminary budget draft: July 15
3. Cross-functional review & iteration: Aug 1 - Sep 15
4. Final budget sign-off: Oct 1 (Board materials to be prepared by Oct 10)
5. Rolling forecast updates: monthly, due 5 business days after month close

Inputs and assumptions:

- Revenue drivers: hosted API usage (tokens), dedicated reserved capacity contracts (committed GPU-hours), private deployment licensing and support fees, add-on services.
- Cost drivers: GPU capacity, cloud egress, instance hours, SRE & support headcount, licensing, model-related inference costs (model hosting fees).

Forecast accuracy targets:

- Revenue variance vs. actual: <= 5% quarterly
- Opex variance vs. budget: <= 7% quarterly
- Capital variance vs. plan: <= 10% annually

Ownership and approvals:

- Department budgets prepared by managers, validated by FP&A, approved by function leads, final approval by CFO.
- Exceptions above $2M CAPEX require CFO + CEO approval.

2) Procurement procedures (purchase to pay):

Policy summary:
- All purchases must follow vendor onboarding, approved budget authority, and contract review rules. Procurement thresholds below are gross value per fiscal year or per single-sourced agreement.

Approval matrix (summary):

| Amount (USD) | Required Approver(s) | Procurement Involvement |
|--------------|----------------------|-------------------------|
| <= 5,000     | Requester manager    | Optional                |
| 5,001 - 50,000 | Director             | Procurement review      |
| 50,001 - 250,000 | VP + Procurement   | Procurement lead required |
| 250,001 - 2,000,000 | CFO + Procurement | Strategic sourcing required |
| > 2,000,000 | CFO + CEO + Board (if multi-year) | Strategic sourcing & legal review |

Vendor onboarding checklist:

1. Vendor profile created in Procurement system (fields: legal name, tax ID, W-9/W-8, primary contact, payment terms).
2. Security and compliance assessment: If vendor will process customer data or have network access, route to Security for SOC2/ISO evidence and Data Protection Addendum (DPA).
3. Risk review (third-party risk questionnaire for > $50k per year).
4. PO issuance and 3-way match on invoice, goods receipt, and PO.

Preferred procurement workflow (step-by-step):

1. Requester creates Purchase Requisition (PR) in procurement tool with business justification and budget code.
2. Manager approves requisition verifying budget availability.
3. Procurement team completes sourcing and vendor checks; negotiates terms.
4. Legal reviews contract if any contractual terms apply (see contracts section).
5. Finance issues PO and captures accounting treatment.
6. Receipt of goods/services triggers invoice approval and payment per payment terms (standard 30 net unless negotiated).

Payment terms, discounts, and exceptions:

- Standard net terms: Net 30. Preferred vendors may be negotiated to Net 45 or Net 60 for strategic partners, with CFO pre-approval.
- Early payment discounts: Teams should evaluate 2%/10 net 30 deals when working capital allows.
- Exceptions: Any non-standard payment or payment in crypto requires CFO and Legal approval.

3) Contracts and legal process (contract lifecycle):

Scope and objectives:

- Ensure consistent contract review, version control, signature authority, and timely execution while mitigating legal and commercial risk.

Contract types covered:

- Customer agreements (SaaS terms, Dedicated/Private deployment contracts), vendor agreements, NDAs, SOWs, reseller/partner agreements, licensing and SaaS integrations.

Standard templates and guardrails:

- Use approved templates stored in Legal Templates space. Key pre-approved deviations: payment terms up to Net 60, indemnity caps up to annual fees, and standard data processing addenda. Any deviation outside guardrails requires Legal escalation.

Contract review workflow (numbered steps):

1. Initiator chooses template and fills key commercial fields in the Contract Request Form (CRF).
2. Legal intake triage within 2 business days; assign priority (Standard, Expedited, Executive).
3. Legal negotiates commercial terms with the counterparty; Procurement supports vendor-side negotiations if procurement-led.
4. Final approved contract routed for signature.

Signature authority matrix:

- Up to $100k ARR or contract value: Head of Sales or Head of Procurement (if vendor).
- $100k - $1M: VP-level review + Legal sign-off; signer: VP or CFO.
- >$1M: CFO and General Counsel sign; Board approval required for multi-year agreements exceeding $5M total commitment.

Contract repository and versioning:

- All executed contracts must be uploaded into the central contract repository (ContractSafe) with metadata: counterparty, start/end dates, contract value, renewal terms, owner, and related PO.
- Renewal notifications: Automated reminders at 90/60/30 days before contract expiration to contract owner and legal.

4) Revenue recognition & billing policies (revrec):

Overview and guiding principle:

- Revenue recognition follows ASC 606 principles (identify contract, performance obligations, allocate transaction price, recognize as obligations are satisfied). The playbook provides practical mechanics for hosted API usage, reserved capacity contracts, and multi-element arrangements (e.g., support + deployment).

Common revenue scenarios and treatment:

1. Hosted API (usage-based): Revenue recognized as usage occurs. Tokens consumed in period are recognized as revenue in the same period; deferred revenue captures advance prepayments/credits.
2. Dedicated (reserved capacity) contracts: If customer prepays or commits to a monthly committed fee, recognize on a straight-line basis over the committed service period unless distinct performance obligations require different schedules.
3. Private deployments and license + support: Distinguish license (if perpetual vs. term) and support; recognize license up-front only if it transfers a right to use distinct from ongoing obligations and GAAP permits, otherwise amortize over the support period.
4. Multi-element arrangements: Allocate transaction price using relative standalone selling prices and recognize each element when satisfied.

Billing and invoicing cadence:

- Standard billing terms: Monthly invoicing in arrears for usage or monthly recurring fees. Annual contracts may be invoiced monthly or annually per negotiated terms.
- Invoices should include: contract ID, period covered, line-item usage/units, unit price, taxes, and payment instructions.
- Dispute handling: Customer disputes must be logged in billing system; business and finance will resolve within 14 business days.

Revenue controls and month-end checklist:

- Verify deferred revenue roll-forward and reconcile to billing ledger.
- Perform contract completeness checks: confirm active contract list matches billed customers and pricing matrix.
- Spot-check revenue for large variances (>5% of MRR or > $25k) and route for controller review.

Revenue recognition sign-offs:

- Monthly close owner: Accounting Controller.
- Material judgments (new contract types, unusual arrangements): Controller + Finance Director + Legal must document accounting memo and obtain CFO sign-off.

5) Exceptions, escalations, and audit evidence:

- Any exception to contract templates, procurement thresholds, or revrec policy must be captured in an exception form and approved by the Controller and General Counsel.
- Audit evidence to collect per transaction: executed contract, PO, invoice, proof of delivery (service logs or usage report), and GL posting reference.

6) Operational tools, templates, and artifacts:

- Contract Request Form (CRF): template file in Legal Templates (link: /confluence/legal/templates/crf).
- Purchase Requisition template: procurement tool default form.
- RevRec checklist: spreadsheet (link: /confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-checklist).
- Standard contract templates: SaaS Master Agreement, Dedicated/Reserved Capacity Addendum, DPA, SOW template.

Appendix A - Quick procedures (cheat-sheet):

A1. Quick purchase (<$5k): manager approval -> PO optional -> payment on invoice.
A2. Medium purchase ($5k - $250k): create PR -> procurement review -> legal if contract -> PO -> goods receipt -> 3-way match invoice.
A3. Large or strategic (> $250k): notify Procurement & Legal at RFP stage -> negotiate T&Cs -> CFO involvement for signature authority.

Appendix B - Sample revenue recognition entries (illustrative):

- Usage-based revenue (monthly): Dr Accounts Receivable; Cr Revenue (usage) for recognized amount. For prepayments: Dr Cash; Cr Deferred Revenue; later Dr Deferred Revenue; Cr Revenue as usage occurs.

Appendix C - Common FAQs:

Q: Who signs NDAs?
A: NDAs under $50k exposure can be signed by Head of Partnerships; all others require Legal sign-off.

Q: What if procurement needs faster turnaround for a vendor trial?
A: Raise an expedited intake with Procurement and Legal; label CRF as Expedited and provide business justification; Procurement SLA for expedited reviews is 3 business days.

Change history and governance:

- This document is maintained by Finance - Contract & Revenue Ops. Major changes (policy changes, thresholds, or accounting treatment updates) require Controller + General Counsel + CFO approval and will be communicated via Finance All-Hands and Confluence update.

Related references (policy & templates):
